title: Pickled cherry tomatoes with goat's cheese and bread

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Vinegar, sugar, fresh vegetables, dill, olive oil, a crusty loaf and goat's cheese are all plain home ingredients.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including a 150g log of soft goat's cheese, is an everyday supermarket buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, a board and a bowl, and the technique is simple slicing and tossing.

works.reason: The vinegar, salt and sugar quick pickle, drained and dressed with oil, makes a sensible quantity of tomatoes, cheese and bread for four as a snack.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is believable for halving the tomatoes, slicing the cucumber, onion and bread and spreading the cheese, and the 15 minute cook time matches the unattended pickling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the dill, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted apart from water appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A fresh, sharp, no-cook cherry tomato pickle suits late June, and the tomatoes are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Bread with goat's cheese and a heap of pickled vegetables is a satisfying, real-food snack a family would make again.
